evaluations.bottleneck: Before the Penn Treebank, large-scale statistical parsing and POS tagging were impractical because there was no large, consistently hand-annotated English corpus to train and evaluate on.
Before the Europarl corpus, training statistical machine translation systems was impractical because large sentence-aligned parallel corpora for European language pairs were scarce.
Before Common Crawl, obtaining web-scale text for language modeling was impractical because crawling and hosting billions of web pages was beyond most research groups.
Before the One Billion Word Benchmark, comparing large-scale language models was impractical because there was no single large, standardized held-out benchmark corpus.
Before BookCorpus, pretraining on long coherent narrative text was impractical because freely available book-length corpora of thousands of unpublished novels did not exist in one dataset.
Before Bayes' theorem, updating beliefs from evidence was impractical in a principled way because there was no formal rule for inverting conditional probabilities.

Q8.evidence: Bayes' theorem became foundational far beyond its original setting, underpinning statistics, machine learning, medical testing, and signal processing, though the Transformer itself is trained by gradient optimization rather than Bayesian inference.
Q8.falsification: This pass dies if the theorem's use remained confined to its original doctrine-of-chances context with no cross-field adoption.
Q8.source: An Essay towards solving a Problem in the Doctrine of Chances

evaluations.bottleneck: Before Cayley's matrix algebra, composing and manipulating systems of linear transformations was impractical because there was no compact notation or calculus for arrays of coefficients as single objects.

Q7.evidence: The Transformer's core computation is expressed entirely as standard matrix operations, notably Attention(Q,K,V) = softmax(QK^T/sqrt(d_k))V, which any practitioner can invoke as a module without re-deriving linear algebra.
Q7.falsification: This pass dies if the Transformer's operations could not be expressed or implemented as standard matrix multiplications.

Q8.evidence: Matrix algebra spread from pure mathematics into physics, engineering, economics, computer graphics, and statistics long before it became the working language of neural network computation.
Q8.falsification: This pass dies if matrix methods had remained a niche notation inside pure mathematics with no uptake in other fields.
Q8.source: A Memoir on the Theory of Matrices

evaluations.bottleneck: Before the Boltzmann distribution, assigning probabilities to states by their energy was impossible in a principled form because statistical mechanics had no exponential law relating state probability to energy and temperature.

Q8.evidence: The Boltzmann form migrated from gas physics into machine learning as the softmax function and into statistical models such as Boltzmann machines, far outside its home field of thermodynamics.
Q8.falsification: This pass dies if the exponential energy-probability form had never been adopted outside physics, in particular not as softmax in neural networks.
Q8.source: Studien über das Gleichgewicht der lebendigen Kraft zwischen bewegten materiellen Punkten

evaluations.bottleneck: Before the GeForce 256, consumer graphics acceleration was impractical as a general compute substrate because GPUs lacked integrated transform-and-lighting hardware and a path toward programmable parallel processors.
Before arXiv, rapid dissemination of preprints was impractical for most researchers because circulation depended on postal mail and institutional preprint lists with weeks of delay.
Before Amazon EC2, elastic compute on demand was impractical for most teams because obtaining servers required capital purchase and provisioning lead times of weeks.
Before Broadbent's filter model, selective attention had no testable mechanistic account because psychology lacked a model of how one input channel is selected and others are blocked.

Before Hubel and Wiesel's receptive-field work, how visual cortex extracts features was unknown because no one had mapped single neurons' responses to oriented edges and hierarchical feature structure.

Before the IBM Models, machine translation by learned word alignment was impractical because there was no probabilistic framework for estimating translation and alignment probabilities from parallel text.
Before Posner's cueing paradigm, covert shifts of visual attention could not be measured because there was no experimental design separating attentional orienting from eye movements.

Before Glorot initialization, training deep networks with saturating activations was impractical because randomly scaled initial weights caused activations and gradients to vanish or explode across layers.
Before the Adam optimizer, training large neural networks robustly was impractical for many practitioners because stochastic gradient descent required extensive per-problem learning-rate tuning.

Q7.evidence: Adam became the default off-the-shelf optimizer invoked as a standard module, and the original Transformer was itself trained with Adam (beta1=0.9, beta2=0.98) under a warmup learning-rate schedule.
Q7.falsification: This pass dies if the Transformer had not in fact been trained with Adam or if Adam had not become a standard reusable optimizer in mainstream frameworks.

evaluations.bottleneck: Before the perceptron, machines that learn a classifier from examples were impractical because there was no implemented learning rule that adjusted weights automatically from labeled data.

Q2.evidence: The perceptron demonstrated a working learn-from-examples machine and launched the neural-network research program whose descendants include the multilayer networks from which the Transformer was built.
Q2.falsification: This pass dies if the perceptron had remained an isolated curiosity that seeded no continuing neural-network research line.
Q2.source: The Perceptron: A Probabilistic Model for Information Storage and Organization in the Brain

evaluations.bottleneck: Before the neural probabilistic language model, statistical language modeling was crippled by the curse of dimensionality because n-gram models treated words as discrete symbols with no notion of similarity between them.

Q11.evidence: The line from this paper runs directly through distributed-representation research and embedding methods into the Transformer's architecture, whose first operation is a learned embedding lookup for every token.
Q11.falsification: This pass dies if a documented alternative lineage shows Transformer embeddings derived independently with no connection to the distributed-representation tradition this paper started.

Q2.evidence: Bengio et al.'s model learned continuous distributed word representations jointly with the language model, opening the entire embedding-based research space that word2vec, and later the Transformer's learned token embeddings, grew from.
Q2.falsification: This pass dies if learned continuous word representations had not propagated beyond this paper into mainstream NLP practice.

Q6.evidence: The paper supplied the deliberate design model the field adopted: represent each word as a learned real-valued feature vector and compute sequence probability with a neural network over those vectors, the same embedding-first design the Transformer uses for its inputs.
Q6.falsification: This pass dies if the Transformer's input representations owed nothing to the learned distributed-representation model this paper introduced.
